name: Catalytic Aerosol Mortar CAM-3 'Lungful'
description: The CAM-3 operates by firing a compressed canister that ruptures at a programmable altitude, releasing a precisely calibrated aerosol suspension of catalytic oxidizing agents. Upon dispersion, a secondary delayed-ignition charge ignites the cloud, producing a deflagration wave tuned to propagate through enclosed spaces with maximum pressure efficiency. The mortar itself is a stubby, break-action single-shot tube with a digital fuse programmer embedded in the grip — operators dial in burst height, dispersion radius, and ignition delay in seconds.
specifications:
weight: 4.1 kg loaded
length: 61 cm
effective range: 40��180 m
blast radius: 8–14 m depending on enclosure geometry
canister capacity: Single shot, break-action reload
fuse delay range: 0.3–6.0 seconds
dispersion modes: Point burst, Wide-area fog, Directional fan
tactical_use: Primarily deployed for building clearance and tunnel engagements where conventional fragmentation is tactically wasteful. Operators fire a round through a doorway or ventilation shaft, letting the cloud settle before detonation — the pressure wave follows corridors and corners in ways solid explosives cannot. Anti-personnel at close range; anti-materiel in confined server rooms or fabrication floors where the overpressure destroys unshielded electronics.
cultural_context: The CAM-3 has a grim reputation in GLMZ's underground circuits as the weapon of choice for corporate extraction teams conducting 'structural audits' — euphemism for eliminating squatter communities in reclaimed industrial zones. Street gangs fear it disproportionately because it offers no warning and no cover. Owning one marks a person as either deeply connected to military supply chains or deeply dangerous to approach.
known_users: Black-market arms brokers who don't use what they sell
Tunnel-network enforcers in the Undercroft districts
story_hooks: A CAM-3 canister with a tampered fuse is found in a residential block's HVAC system — the ignition timer is set for the building's peak occupancy hour.
A runner is hired to retrieve a stolen shipment of CAM-3 canisters; the job goes sideways when they discover the 'client' is the same extraction team that cleared their old neighborhood.
An ARCTURUS whistleblower claims the CAM-3's aerosol formula was field-tested on civilian populations before military sale — and has the atmospheric sensor logs to prove it.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutally compact break-action mortar with a pronounced stubby barrel and reinforced breech. The silhouette reads as a sawed-off grenade launcher crossed with a flare gun—all business, no elegance. The grip dominates the lower half, thickened by the integrated digital fuse programmer module.
physical_description.dimensions: 61 cm length overall; barrel bore 40 mm; grip width 8 cm; depth 12 cm at the breech assembly
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but balanced—4.1 kg feels substantial in the hand without being unwieldy. The weight sits slightly forward in the barrel, encouraging a stable two-handed firing posture.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer composite frame with steel barrel liner and aluminum breech block. Internal pressure vessel is hardened steel.
physical_description.finish: Matte tactical polymer—olive-drab green base with charcoal accents. Steel barrel shows light oxidation and micro-scarring from pressurized canister ejection cycles.
physical_description.color_scheme: Sage green polymer body; gunmetal gray barrel and breech hardware; digital display backlit in acidic amber on the grip module
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured rubberized polymer with raised grip panels; the fuse programmer module beneath has a slight dimpled finish for tactile button feedback. Bare aluminum charging lever on the side.
distinctive_features: Prominent break-action lever extending from the breech—chunky, mechanical, requires significant leverage to cycle
3x3 cm digital LCD screen recessed into the grip showing altitude/delay/dispersion mode readouts in glowing amber text
Four rubber-capped pressure vent ports along the barrel (2 per side) for canister bleed-off
Charging handle with witness holes for round confirmation
Integrated accessory rail (Picatinny) along the top, typically bare or bearing only a simple backup iron sight
Faint engraved serial plate (ARCTURUS model stamp) on the left breech face
Slight carbon scoring and powder residue buildup around the barrel muzzle—typical field condition
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS stamp in sans-serif font on the left side of the breech block, just above the break-action lever. Small QR-code engraving (unreadable without magnification) adjacent to the serial plate.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but well-maintained. Polymer shows scuff marks and minor impact scarring consistent with tactical equipment transport. Barrel interior cleaned regularly; breech seals show light wear. Digital display occasionally exhibits minor pixel dropout from thermal cycling.
